_comment: Config for the weekly sharded mutation run.
SCOPE: RunnerCore + Core. ~10,200 LOC, ~1,700 mutants, 8 shards of ~60
minutes. Widened after run 3 came back green at this tool's first fully
successful sweep -- 122 killed, 23 survivors, 84%, with 64 phantom mutants
filtered out -- which is the condition the previous config named for widening.
SHARD COUNT IS SET BY FIXED COST, NOT BY MUTANTS. Measured across run 3's three
shards: ~29 minutes of fixed overhead each (a cold build of the project inside
Muter's copy, plus the unmutated baseline run) and only ~9.8 seconds per mutant
after that. So shards are cheap in wall-clock and expensive in compute, and the
curve flattens fast: 1,700 mutants cost ~84 min over 5 shards, ~63 over 8, ~56
over 10. Eight is where the marginal shard stops buying much.
CORE SURVIVORS CARRY A CAVEAT THAT RUNNERCORE'S DO NOT. The suite skips
APITests -- unavoidably, since it dominates the runtime -- and Core is exercised
through it. Measured by static reference: 89% of Core's LOC is reachable from
CoreTests or WorkerTests, 5% only from APITests, and 6% from no test at all. So
a Core survivor in one of those APITests-only files may be an artefact of the
skip rather than a hole, exactly as a missing interpreter would be. Check such a
survivor against the full suite before writing a test for it. RunnerCore has no
such caveat: its covering tests all run here.
WORKER IS STILL EXCLUDED, and for a reason that is the same shape. The baseline
fix that made run 3 possible is --skip WorkerTests/, which drops the 48
timing-sensitive sandbox and timeout tests. Mutating Sources/Worker while those
do not run would report survivors in precisely the code they cover. Adding
Worker means first making that suite survivable in this configuration, which is
a separate problem from widening scope.
--skip WorkerTests/ removes exactly the 48 tests of the WorkerTests SUITE, not
the 343 of the WorkerTests MODULE: ids read `WorkerTests.WorkerTests/...` for
the suite and `WorkerTests.CppNativeGradingTests/...` for its siblings, so the
trailing slash discriminates. That keeps the 295 sibling tests that actually
cover RunnerCore -- notebook extraction, script classification, the R and Lua
runtimes -- while dropping the suite that holds the timing-sensitive sandbox and
timeout tests and spawns concurrent worker daemons. Running those in one process
beside CoreTests on a 2-core runner is a configuration nothing else exercises:
CI runs the targets as separate jobs, and on a laptop the interpreter-dependent
tests skip, which is why the same command passes locally with 760 green.
--skip ZipProcessEnvironmentTests IS NOW LOAD-BEARING, where under the previous
RunnerCore-only scope it was merely prudent. Muter writes
`import class Foundation.ProcessInfo` into every file it mutates before the
baseline runs, and that suite scans Sources/Core files for `Process(`
constructions -- so with Core in scope the preamble reaches the files it reads.
The general rule: a test asserting on the TEXT of a file under mutation cannot
coexist with mutation, and has no mutants worth killing anyway.
-Xswiftc -no-warnings-as-errors IS LOAD-BEARING. The package builds with
.treatAllWarnings(as: .error), and RemoveSideEffects deletes the USE of a
binding, leaving `let x = ...` unused -- a warning, therefore an error,
therefore a copy that does not compile and a shard that yields zero mutants.
APIServer is excluded permanently, not pending: 94k LOC, ~15,700 mutants that
must be graded by APITests, ~1,712h serial -- ~96% of the tree's cost for its
least informative mutants. Triage scales with SURVIVORS, and a report nobody can
read is worse than none because it looks like coverage.
